name: cross-language-collision-freedom
body:
Cross-language module and symbol FQN collisions become impossible because each language is a disjoint root namespace: two same-named modules or symbols in different languages render under different roots and both survive. The ingestor's cross-language silent shadowing therefore disappears.

The WITHIN-language collision handling is retained unchanged and is explicitly in scope: a module whose FQN is claimed by a struct or function of the same language (legal Java package/type name sharing, e.g. `pkg.A` the package and `pkg.A` the class) is still shadowed by the type, counted in `shadowed_modules`, and logged (`src/main.rs`: "module(s) shadowed by a type of the same name"); a function whose FQN a struct claimed is still shadowed and counted in `shadowed_functions`; a genuine same-kind Struct/Function collision still panics (`claim`, `src/ingest.rs:88-96`). Language rooting removes only the CROSS-language case.

Acceptance: a scan mixing a Rust module `apg` and a Python package `apg` yields both `rust.apg` and `py.apg` (today the second silently shadows the first); a Java package/type same-name case in one language still shadows with the counter incremented; a same-language same-kind duplicate still panics; no cross-language module is counted as shadowed.
